title: Karavan, files and dev mode
summary: A visual designer over plain YAML, what Saved and Committed mean, the delete trap, and dev mode versus a packaged image.

steps.title: A designer over plain files
body: **Karavan** is a browser-based designer for Camel (Kaoto is a similar one inside VS Code). A Karavan
**project** is just a folder of files:
```text
catalogue-integration/
application.properties        configuration (like appsettings.json)
get-book.camel.yaml            one route file per operation
default-error-handler.camel.yaml
docker-compose.yaml            how the project runs as a container (port, image)
openapi.json                   the contract, if contract-first
The canvas is only a **view** of those YAML files: every box is one YAML block, every form field one key, and an
empty field writes nothing. There is no hidden binary model, so everything you draw can be reviewed as a normal
Git diff. A project becomes one Git folder, one image and one running service, so make it one per **business
domain** (catalogue, orders), not one per endpoint.

steps.title: Saved, committed, built
body: Three different states, often confused:
- **Saved**: stored in Karavan's own database. Every change is saved **immediately**. Nobody else sees it.
- **Committed**: pushed to Git, the source of truth. Reviewers, pipelines and colleagues see it.
- **Built**: an image built **from a Git commit**. Anything only *saved* is not in it.
Two traps follow:
- **Undo** in the Diff view means "revert this file to the last commit". Before the first commit there is
nothing to revert to: it wipes the file.
- The **delete** button on a selected step acts immediately and is saved at once. Delete a `setVariable` that
later steps read, or a `direct:` route that other routes call, and the project still saves and may even start.
It breaks at runtime.
So: commit at every working milestone. From then on Undo is a real safety net, like `git restore`.

steps.prompt: A colleague deleted the `setVariable isbn` step by accident and committed. The route still starts, but the backend now logs requests for `/api/books/`. Why?
options: `${variable.isbn}` evaluates to empty when the variable is never set, so the URL ends in an empty segment
Karavan rejected the change and kept the old version
steps.explain: Simple does not fail on a missing variable. Review diffs for removed steps, and test the happy path after every change.

steps.title: Dev mode versus a packaged image
body: **Run** in Karavan starts a **dev-mode** container: Camel JBang reads your files straight from Karavan,
downloads the components your routes use from Maven Central at startup, and starts Camel. No build. Like
`dotnet watch run`.
- **Reload** (hot reload) swaps the routes inside the running container in seconds. It needs the project's
management port enabled, and it cannot apply everything: changes to `application.properties` or new
dependencies need a full **restart** (delete the container, Run again).
- A **packaged image** is built from a Git commit with every dependency inside (Karavan uses Maven and Jib).
It starts faster, uses a fraction of the memory, needs no internet at startup, and is what production runs.
Like `dotnet publish` plus a container image.

steps.title: Find what a deletion broke
prompt: Before deleting a step, you want a check that finds dangling references. The tests declare:
record Step(string Name, string[] Sets, string[] Reads, string? CallsDirect);
record RouteDef(string Id, string? FromDirect, List<Step> Steps);
`Sets` / `Reads` are variable names; `CallsDirect` is the name of a `direct:` endpoint the step calls (or null); `FromDirect` is the direct name a route consumes (or null for HTTP routes).
Write `List<string> Problems(List<RouteDef> routes)` returning, in route order and then step order:
- `"{routeId}/{stepName}: reads '{v}' before anything sets it"` for each read of a variable not set by an **earlier** step of the same route;
- `"{routeId}/{stepName}: calls direct:{name}, which no route consumes"`.
solution: var consumed = routes.Where(r => r.FromDirect != null).Select(r => r.FromDirect!).ToHashSet();
if (!set.Contains(v)) problems.Add($"{route.Id}/{step.Name}: reads '{v}' before anything sets it");
problems.Add($"{route.Id}/{step.Name}: calls direct:{step.CallsDirect}, which no route consumes");
hints: Collect every `FromDirect` into a set first.
Per route, walk the steps keeping a set of variables set so far; check reads before adding this step's sets.

Dojo.Eq("deleted setVariable and deleted route", new List<string>
"get-book/to-stock: calls direct:checkStock, which no route consumes",
var dojoOrder = new List<RouteDef> { new("r", null, new() { S("use", reads: new[] { "x" }), S("set", sets: new[] { "x" }) }) };
Dojo.Eq("setting a variable after reading it is still a problem", new List<string> { "r/use: reads 'x' before anything sets it" }, Problems(dojoOrder));
